_comment: Azure Machine Learning compute VM size allow-list.
WHY THIS EXISTS: this is the single largest hole the custom role leaves
open. ROLE_ALLOWED_PROVIDERS includes Microsoft.MachineLearningServices,
and the role builder expands every provider to '<provider>/*' - so the
role grants workspaces/computes/write. That operation creates a GPU
cluster at ANY size. RBAC cannot see the vmSize in the request body, so
without this definition the role can stand up an ND96 cluster and the
only thing that notices is the invoice.
WHY A CUSTOM DEFINITION: no built-in restricts AML compute VM SKUs.
Verified 2026-09-25 - all 30 built-ins in the Machine Learning category
were enumerated; they cover private link, public network access, local
auth, CMK, user-assigned identity, approved registries/modules/
environments and compute idle shutdown. Not one of them constrains the
VM size. 'Azure Machine Learning Computes should have local
authentication methods disabled' (7804b5c7-01dc-4723-969b-ae300cc07ff1)
is the closest neighbour: same resource type, and it is the shape
reference for the two structural decisions below.
MODE IS 'All' AND THAT IS MANDATORY. workspaces/computes is a CHILD
resource type. Indexed only evaluates resource types that support tags
and location, so an Indexed definition here would match NOTHING - it
would deploy cleanly, report 100% compliant, and enforce nothing at all.
That is a worse outcome than having no policy, because it looks like a
control. Microsoft's own built-in for this same type uses mode All.
WHY THE computeType GATE: workspaces/computes is a polymorphic type.
AmlCompute and ComputeInstance carry properties.properties.vmSize;
AKS, Databricks, Synapse Spark, HDInsight and attached VM computes do
not. Without the gate this rule reaches resources whose payload has no
such path, which is both wrong and noisy. The gate is copied from the
built-in named above.
ABOUT THE DEFAULT LIST: it deliberately excludes EVERY GPU size - the
whole NC, ND and NV series - and every large memory-optimised size. That
is the point of the ceiling, not an oversight. Adding a GPU size to
AML_ALLOWED_VM_SIZES is a deliberate cost decision and should be made by
whoever owns the budget, not by whoever needs the cluster today.
ALIASES VERIFIED against the live provider:
Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/computes/vmSize
(defaultPath properties.properties.vmSize)
Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/computes/computeType
NOTE ON exists: vmSize is not present on every compute payload even
within the gated compute types, so the value test is guarded by an
exists check and an omitted property is not treated as a violation.

properties.displayName: Azure ML compute must use an approved VM size
properties.description: Denies or audits Azure Machine Learning AmlCompute clusters and ComputeInstances created with a VM size outside the approved list. The default list is CPU-only: GPU sizes are excluded because a GPU cluster is a committed-spend decision, not an innovation one.

metadata.description: Audit reports without blocking. Deny blocks the deployment.

metadata.displayName: Allowed Azure ML compute VM sizes
metadata.description: Permitted vmSize values for AmlCompute and ComputeInstance. The default is CPU-only and excludes every GPU size (NC, ND and NV series). Adding a GPU size is a deliberate cost decision.
